newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis seen stronger than SMI in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Novartis seen stronger than SMI in 1997.

text.p: Shares in Swiss pharma giant Novartis AG, created by the merger of Sandoz AG and Ciba-Geigy AG, should rise by 13 to 16 percent in 1997, analysts said.
Expectations for Novartis in 1997 were somewhat stronger than an average 10 percent forecast in a recent Reuter poll for the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), of which Novartis makes up 26 percent.
Analysts forecast a strong upside potential for Novartis based on cost savings from the merger as well as new products expected to come on the market next year.

Andreas Vogler, head of Swiss equities research at SBC Warburg in Zurich, set a 1997 target price of 1,750 Swiss francs per Novartis registered in the bi-weekly Swiss business paper Finanz und Wirtschaft.
This would be a rise of 16.5 percent from the Novartis opening of 1,502 francs on Monday, its first day of trade on the Swiss Exchange.
"We expect profit growth next year of around 20 percent, which together with the better than average quality of profit should lead to clear gains by the share," he told the newspaper.
Other analysts put price expectations at between 1,650 and 1,700 Swiss francs, a gain of 10 to 13 percent.
"Novartis has a strong upside potential," said John Murphy from Goldman Sachs, which does not have a target price for the share.
Goldman Sachs has put Novartis on its priority list for 1997, one of only two shares from about 20 European drug sector companies to achieve the ranking.
"They are looking at strong savings and new products in the pipeline in 1997," Murphy said of Novartis.
Novartis estimates the merger will save about two billion Swiss francs over three years. They plan to cut the combined workforce by about 10 percent, or 12,000 jobs.
